method: Callgrind Ir counts executed instructions, not hardware CPU cycles or elapsed-time shares. Exclusive function counts reconcile with the profiler total; inclusive edge costs overlap. DHAT replaces allocator routines and records requested heap bytes, blocks, and lifetimes by allocation stack; these bytes are allocation traffic, not RSS. Instrumented elapsed times are excluded from performance comparisons.
hardware_counters: No hardware CPU counters were collected; Callgrind Ir is not CPU cycles or elapsed-time share.
selection: Current-Relar application profiles use exact final timed binaries. Baseline/Rust application profiles and storage probes reuse exact unchanged artifacts from integration profiling. Superseded current-Relar integration profiles remain in the raw archive but are not used for final tables.

execution_after.policy: all engines inherit the same harness environment without per-engine overrides; CPython -I ignores Python environment settings; only this runtime-relevant allowlist is recorded

storage_mechanism.optional_wrappers: At size N the present integer and present Leaf optionals lose exactly 2*N allocations. The remaining N Leaf records still allocate.
storage_mechanism.object_requests: Raw DHAT stacks show old generic object requests of 88 bytes; new Leaf requests are 24 bytes, four-field Record requests 48 bytes, and two-field tuple requests 32 bytes. Container capacity growth also affects total traffic.
storage_mechanism.limits: Requested allocator bytes and peak live heap are not RSS; the synthetic storage fixture is a mechanism probe, not an elapsed-time application benchmark.
